overview.title: Portfolio Overview
overview.purpose: Executive fleet view of health, performance, availability, work backlog, financial exposure and maintenance mix.
overview.use: Start with the AI Executive Command Briefing for the day's ranked decisions, then the six KPI cards for portfolio state, then use site and maintenance drill-downs for the underlying cause.

kpis.name: Fleet Health Index
kpis.formula: Simple average of PLANTS[].healthScore across all plants. Each plant's healthScore = 58 + (PR% − 90) × 7 + (Availability% − 96) × 4 + a small random adjustment (−6 to +6), clamped to the range 41–98.
kpis.rules: This is a demo linear formula, not a governed multi-factor composite — it uses only PR and Availability as inputs, plus randomised noise. It does not separately weight critical-risk exposure, backlog or RUL as distinct components. The card's "▲ 4 pts vs last quarter" delta is fixed display text, not a computed period-over-period comparison.
kpis.meaning: Higher indicates a plant combining strong PR and availability; treat the exact number as illustrative, not an audited composite score.

kpis.name: Portfolio PR
kpis.formula: Simple average of PLANTS[].pr across all 12 plants.
kpis.rules: This is an unweighted average of each plant's static demo PR value — not an energy-weighted or irradiance-normalised calculation. The "▲ 0.8 pt vs baseline" delta is fixed display text, not computed.
kpis.meaning: Average of the plants' displayed PR figures; not capacity- or energy-weighted.

kpis.name: Availability
kpis.formula: Simple average of PLANTS[].availability across all 12 plants.
kpis.rules: Unweighted average of each plant's static demo availability value. The "— in line with SLA" label is fixed display text, not evaluated against any actual SLA threshold.
kpis.meaning: Average of the plants' displayed availability figures; not capacity-weighted.

kpis.name: Open Work Orders
kpis.formula: Count of records in ALL_WOS whose status is not "Closed" and not "Completed".
kpis.rules: Pools work orders across Corrective, Preventive, Adaptive and Predictive maintenance.

kpis.name: Revenue at Risk
kpis.formula: A fixed constant, ₹41,800,000. The code adds RISK_ASSETS.reduce((s,r)=>s+(1-r.riskScore)*0,0), but that term is multiplied by 0 and always evaluates to zero, so the displayed value never actually varies with risk data.
kpis.rules: Not currently computed from live risk, generation-loss or tariff data despite the label. The same value also feeds the "Revenue exposure" figure in the AI Executive Command Briefing above the KPI cards.
kpis.meaning: Illustrative placeholder value only in the current build.

kpis.name: CO₂ Avoided (annualized)
kpis.formula: TOTAL_MW × 1550 × 0.79, explicitly commented "illustrative" in the source code.
kpis.scope: Static illustrative calculation from installed capacity
kpis.rules: Uses installed capacity and two fixed constants (an assumed generation-hours factor and an illustrative emission factor) — not actual metered generation or a governed grid emission factor.
kpis.meaning: Illustrative estimate only; not derived from real generation data in the current build.

kpis.name: Priority Actions (Command Briefing)
kpis.formula: Sum of four counts: open Critical-priority work orders + overdue Preventive tasks + spare-part SKUs at/below reorder point + assets with High risk band.
kpis.rules: Adds counts from four different domains (maintenance, spares, asset risk) into one number; an item can only be counted once since each source count is disjoint, but the total has no single unit of meaning beyond "things needing a decision today".
kpis.meaning: Complete governed action population assembled from critical work orders, overdue preventive tasks, spares reorder requirements and high-risk assets; use the Actions Required drill-down to inspect every record.

kpis.name: Critical Interventions (Command Briefing)
kpis.formula: Count of work orders in ALL_WOS with priority = "Critical" and status not in (Closed, Completed).
kpis.rules: Same population as the "Critical priority" KPI used on the Work Order Intelligence screen.

kpis.name: Lowest-Performing Site (Command Briefing)
kpis.formula: The plant in PLANTS[] with the lowest .pr value, sorted ascending.
kpis.rules: Ties are broken by array order, not by a secondary tiebreaker field.
kpis.meaning: Points directly at the site most worth opening in Site Performance.

overview.visuals: AI Executive Command Briefing surfaces the day's ranked decisions with quick links; Site Registry shows PR, availability and a calculated Site Health Score derived as the simple average of the governed calculated asset Health Scores for assets at each site; Maintenance Mix shows work-order distribution and proactive share.
overview.data: Plant, Asset Master, telemetry, AI alerts, events, work orders, AI Vision, generation, risk and ESG datasets. Site Health is aggregated from the governed calculated asset Health Scores.
overview.limits: Composite scores are decision aids; validate source data and weighting before external reporting. Several headline figures (Revenue at Risk, CO₂ Avoided, all trend-delta labels) are static or illustrative and do not move with the underlying data in this build — verify before using in an executive readout.

glossary.def: A single 0–100 score meant to summarise how healthy the whole portfolio is; in this build it's a simple two-factor blend of PR and availability, not a governed multi-factor composite.

How efficiently a site converts available sunlight into AC energy, independent of how sunny it was. High availability with low PR usually means soiling, clipping or a sensor/data problem, not downtime.
Whether the equipment was capable of generating, regardless of how much sun there was. Different from PR — a site can be 99% available but still underperform on PR.

The commercial exposure from open critical/high-severity issues over a 30-day window. In this build it is a fixed illustrative number, not a live calculation — treat the concept as real but the figure as a placeholder.
The percentage of work orders that are Preventive, Adaptive or Predictive rather than Corrective — a higher share generally indicates a more mature, less reactive maintenance program.

aivision.title: AI Vision
aivision.purpose: Turns drone, thermal, RGB, mobile or CCTV inspection evidence into prioritised visual findings and linked maintenance action.
aivision.use: Filter by site, defect, severity, capture mode and status; open a finding for evidence and work-order linkage.

kpis.name: Panels inspected
kpis.formula: Σ Panels_Inspected/Modules_Inspected from Vision KPI History; if unavailable, count usable inspection images or inspection records.
kpis.rules: Count only accepted, non-duplicate inspection records; the synthetic fallback is a demo coverage value.
kpis.meaning: Inspection coverage represented in the current dataset.

kpis.name: AI findings
kpis.formula: Count of distinct Vision Findings records; synthetic mode scales representative findings for portfolio demonstration.
kpis.rules: Deduplicate by finding ID and exclude rejected/invalid detections when status exists.
kpis.meaning: Total detected visual anomalies available for review.

kpis.name: Critical defects
kpis.formula: Count of findings where Severity or Risk Level = Critical.
kpis.rules: Only findings classified Critical under the active severity taxonomy are included.

kpis.name: Thermal hotspots
kpis.formula: Count of findings whose defect/finding type contains hotspot or thermal; fallback uses Vision Thermal records.
kpis.rules: Count each distinct finding once even when multiple images support it.

kpis.name: Work orders created
kpis.formula: Count of Vision Work Order Link records, or findings with a linked Work_Order_ID.
kpis.rules: Count distinct linked work-order IDs and exclude blank links.
kpis.meaning: How many findings have progressed into execution.

kpis.name: Revenue at risk
kpis.formula: Σ Annual_Revenue_Risk_INR or equivalent estimated revenue-loss field across findings.
kpis.rules: Exclude duplicate findings for the same defect unless separate loss areas are documented.
kpis.meaning: Estimated annual commercial exposure from visual defects.

aivision.visuals: The gallery shows image evidence, confidence, severity, estimated loss and recommended action.
aivision.data: Vision Inspections, Vision Findings, Vision Images, Vision Thermal, Vision Work Order Link and Vision KPI History.
aivision.limits: Detection confidence is not defect severity; engineer confirmation is required before execution.

workorderintelligence.title: Work Order Command Centre
workorderintelligence.purpose: Governed operational workspace for open work orders, scheduling readiness, SLA exposure, approvals, audit history and ERP/EAM handoff.
workorderintelligence.use: Use tabs to move from command view to ledger, lifecycle, exceptions, audit and transaction status.

kpis.name: Open work orders
kpis.formula: Count of distinct work orders with status other than Closed or Completed.
kpis.rules: Deduplicate by work-order ID across imported and generated records.

kpis.name: Critical priority
kpis.formula: Count of open work orders whose priority = Critical.
kpis.rules: Use the displayed governed priority field; do not infer from colour alone.

kpis.name: Overdue Actions
kpis.formula: Count of open work orders with due date earlier than the current/as-of date.
kpis.rules: Use approved revised due date when present; exclude Closed/Completed.

kpis.name: Ready to schedule
kpis.formula: Count of open work orders meeting the screen readiness rule: required scope/evidence available and not blocked by approval, material or data exceptions.
kpis.rules: A work order is counted once after all configured readiness conditions pass.
kpis.meaning: Demand that can move into crew scheduling.

kpis.name: SLA at risk
kpis.formula: Count of open work orders whose remaining SLA time is within the configured warning threshold or already breached.
kpis.rules: Pause or exclusion rules follow the configured SLA policy.
kpis.meaning: Work likely to miss response/restoration commitments.

kpis.name: ERP/EAM pending
kpis.formula: Count of approved work orders not yet successfully acknowledged by the target ERP/EAM.
kpis.rules: Exclude successfully posted/acknowledged transactions; count latest status per work order.

workorderintelligence.visuals: Command Centre summarises backlog; other tabs expose record detail, lifecycle, exceptions, audit and ERP status.
workorderintelligence.data: Work Orders, approvals, crew/material readiness and integration transaction records.
workorderintelligence.limits: The AIP governs and explains; ERP/EAM remains the transactional system of record.

corrective.title: Corrective Maintenance
corrective.purpose: Tracks reactive maintenance after a fault or failure.
corrective.use: Use trends and work-order rows to reduce restoration time and repeat breakdowns.

kpis.name: Open Work Orders
kpis.formula: Count of CORRECTIVE_WOS records where status = "Open" only.
kpis.rules: This counts only the "Open" status, not "Open + In Progress" or any other non-closed state — In Progress items are shown separately as a sub-label, not included in this count.
kpis.meaning: Backlog of not-yet-started corrective work specifically.

kpis.name: MTTR
kpis.formula: Latest value from MTTR_TREND, a 24-month array pre-generated as 30 − (month_index/23)×11 + a small sine-wave variation + random noise (trending downward by design).
kpis.rules: This is a synthetic illustrative trend, not a live calculation from actual work-order fault-to-restore timestamps.
kpis.meaning: Demo trend value; treat as illustrative, not a computed operational metric.

kpis.name: MTBF
kpis.formula: Latest value from MTBF_TREND, a 24-month array pre-generated as 620 + (month_index/23)×260 + a small sine-wave variation + random noise (trending upward by design).
kpis.rules: This is a synthetic illustrative trend, not a live calculation from actual failure-interval data.
kpis.meaning: Demo trend value; treat as illustrative, not a computed operational metric.

kpis.name: Breakdowns (30d)
kpis.formula: A random integer between 9 and 14, regenerated on each render (rndInt(9,14)).
kpis.rules: Not counted from any breakdown-event dataset in the current build — it is randomised every time the screen renders.
kpis.meaning: Illustrative placeholder only; does not reflect a real trailing-30-day count.

corrective.visuals: MTTR/MTBF trend and corrective work-order table show restoration performance and failure categories.
corrective.data: Corrective work orders, event timestamps and asset operating history.
corrective.limits: MTBF is unreliable for sparse or mixed populations; interpret by asset class.

preventive.title: Preventive Maintenance
preventive.purpose: Tracks fixed-calendar maintenance schedules and compliance.
preventive.use: Review overdue tasks, frequency concentration and due dates.

kpis.name: Scheduled Tasks
kpis.formula: Count of PREVENTIVE_WOS records where status = "Scheduled".
kpis.rules: Distinct PM task/work-order IDs.

kpis.name: Overdue Actions
kpis.formula: Count of PREVENTIVE_WOS records where status = "Overdue".
kpis.rules: Use approved rescheduled date when present.

kpis.name: Upcoming PM Due (30d)
kpis.formula: Count of PREVENTIVE_WOS records whose PM Due Date is after PM_COMPLIANCE_AS_OF and on or before PM_COMPLIANCE_AS_OF + 30 days, excluding Completed/Closed records. Uses pmDueDate/PM_Due_Date with nextDue/Next_Due as fallback.
kpis.scope: Next 30 days from the PM compliance as-of date
kpis.rules: Derived only from loaded Preventive work-order/PM-plan due dates; no hardcoded task count. Completed and closed work are excluded.
kpis.meaning: Near-term preventive workload that will become due within 30 days and requires planning/readiness.

kpis.name: PM Compliance Rate
kpis.formula: On-time completed preventive tasks due as of PM_COMPLIANCE_AS_OF ÷ all preventive tasks due as of PM_COMPLIANCE_AS_OF × 100.
kpis.rules: 0-day tolerance. Completed-late and overdue-open tasks are non-compliant; future scheduled tasks are excluded; missing due-date evidence is excluded from the due population.
kpis.meaning: Share of due preventive maintenance completed on or before its PM Due Date.

preventive.visuals: Frequency-band chart shows cadence; table shows last-done and next-due dates.
preventive.data: Preventive plans and work-order completion records.
preventive.limits: High compliance does not prove maintenance effectiveness; review outcomes separately.

adaptive.title: Adaptive Maintenance
adaptive.purpose: Adjusts maintenance intervals using condition and operating context.
adaptive.use: Review interval compression/extension and condition-triggered interventions.

kpis.name: Assets on Adaptive Schedule
kpis.formula: Count of distinct in-scope assets currently governed by an adaptive interval.
kpis.rules: Count active adaptive assignments only.

kpis.name: Avg. Interval Compression
kpis.formula: 100 × average of (1 − Adaptive_Interval ÷ Fixed_Interval) across asset classes with valid fixed and adaptive interval values.
kpis.rules: Positive means shorter intervals; calculate only where baseline interval > 0.
kpis.meaning: Average increase in maintenance frequency due to condition.

kpis.name: Condition Triggers (30d)
kpis.formula: If an imported trigger-count field exists, sums it across assets; otherwise counts ADAPTIVE_WOS records not in Closed/Completed status.
kpis.rules: The "(30d)" window is a label, not an enforced date filter in the fallback path — the fallback counts all currently-open adaptive work orders, not specifically those from the last 30 days.
kpis.meaning: Volume of active condition-driven schedule activity.

kpis.name: Interventions Avoided
kpis.formula: Average of each asset's interventionsAvoidedPct field where present; if no assets have this field, defaults to a fixed 74%.
kpis.rules: This is a percentage (shown with a % unit on screen), not a count of interventions — a prior description of this as a raw count was incorrect.
kpis.meaning: Higher % indicates more maintenance visits avoided vs. the fixed-calendar baseline.

adaptive.visuals: Interval table explains baseline versus adjusted dates and trigger evidence.
adaptive.data: Condition monitoring, maintenance plans and approvals.
adaptive.limits: Adaptive deferral requires governed safety and statutory constraints.

predictive.title: Predictive Maintenance
predictive.purpose: Forecasts degradation and failure risk from telemetry and history.
predictive.use: Use risk, RUL and lead time to time intervention before failure.

kpis.name: Models in Production
kpis.formula: A hardcoded literal value of 11 in the template — it is not counted from MODEL_REGISTRY or any live model-status data.
kpis.rules: This card never changes regardless of the actual number of Production-status models in the AI Model Registry.
kpis.meaning: Static demo label; cross-check the real count on the AI Model Registry screen instead.

kpis.name: Avg. Detection Lead Time
kpis.formula: A random integer between 9 and 16 days (rndInt(9,16)), or fixed at 3 days while the anomaly demo is active.
kpis.rules: Regenerated randomly on each render — not computed from any alert/failure timestamp data.

kpis.name: False Positive Rate
kpis.formula: A random value between 6% and 11% (rnd(6,11)), regenerated on each render.
kpis.rules: Not computed from any alert-outcome validation data in the current build.

kpis.name: Assets at Critical Risk / Agent Resolution Rate
kpis.formula: Outside the anomaly demo: a random integer between 71 and 86 (rndInt(71,86)), labelled "Agent Resolution Rate %". During the anomaly demo: fixed at the literal value "1", labelled "Assets at Critical Risk".
kpis.rules: Neither state is computed from real agent-resolution or risk data — both are hardcoded/random demo values.
kpis.meaning: Illustrative placeholder only in both states.

predictive.visuals: Risk panels and anomaly workflow show signals, RUL and action path.
predictive.data: Telemetry, events, predictive outputs, model registry and work outcomes.
predictive.limits: RUL is probabilistic and must be interpreted with confidence and consequence.

prescriptive.title: Prescriptive Maintenance
prescriptive.purpose: Compares action alternatives and recommends timing and scope.
prescriptive.use: Review recommendation rationale, confidence, cost and avoided impact.

kpis.name: Repair-Now Recommendations
kpis.formula: Count of active recommendations whose selected action is Repair now.
kpis.rules: Distinct recommendation IDs; exclude accepted/closed items if no longer active.

kpis.name: Agent Accept Rate
kpis.formula: 100 × count(recommendations where accepted = true) ÷ total PRESCRIPTIVE_RECS count.
kpis.rules: The denominator is every recommendation in the dataset, not only ones with a completed accept/reject decision — recommendations with no decision yet are counted as not-accepted in this ratio.
kpis.meaning: Share of all recommendations currently marked accepted.

kpis.name: Est. Cost Avoided
kpis.formula: Σ probability-adjusted deferred-failure cost − recommended-action cost for active/accepted recommendations.
kpis.rules: Do not double count linked recommendations for one event.

kpis.name: Avg. Recommendation Confidence
kpis.formula: Σ recommendation confidence ÷ active recommendations.
kpis.rules: Simple average unless production weighting is configured; exclude missing confidence.

prescriptive.visuals: Recommendation cards compare action, timing, rationale and expected impact.
prescriptive.data: Risk outputs, work history, costs, spares, crew and warranty context.
prescriptive.limits: Recommended action remains advisory until approved.

riskbased.title: Risk-Based Maintenance
riskbased.purpose: Ranks assets by probability and consequence.
riskbased.use: Use the queue to focus resources on the highest composite risk.

kpis.name: Critical-Tier Items
kpis.formula: Count of RISK_QUEUE items where composite > 0.70.
kpis.rules: Use configured tier thresholds and latest score per item.

kpis.name: High-Tier Items
kpis.formula: Count of RISK_QUEUE items where composite is between 0.50 and 0.70.
kpis.rules: Exclude Critical items.

kpis.name: Fleet Avg. Composite Score
kpis.formula: Average of item.composite across RISK_QUEUE, where each item.composite = (Energy_Impact×0.4 + Safety_Risk×0.4 + (11 − Accessibility)×0.2) ÷ 10.
kpis.rules: Accessibility is inverted as (11 − Accessibility) before weighting, so a low accessibility score (hard to reach) increases composite risk — the raw Accessibility field itself is not added directly.
kpis.meaning: Average risk intensity across the open queue, 0–1 scale.

kpis.name: Items in Risk Queue
kpis.formula: Count of distinct active risk-register items awaiting treatment or acceptance.
kpis.rules: Exclude closed/retired items.

riskbased.visuals: Risk matrix and queue show tier, probability, consequence and treatment.
riskbased.data: Asset criticality, failure probability and consequence dimensions.
riskbased.limits: Composite scores depend on governed weights and thresholds.

rcm.title: Reliability-Centered Maintenance
rcm.purpose: Documents strategy selection by asset function, failure mode and consequence.
rcm.use: Review strategy assignments and framework coverage.

kpis.name: Asset Classes Reviewed
kpis.formula: RCM_MATRIX.length — the total number of rows in the static RCM matrix dataset.
kpis.rules: This counts every row in the loaded matrix; it does not distinguish "reviewed" from "not yet reviewed" since the current dataset has no review-status field.
kpis.meaning: Total asset-class/failure-mode combinations documented in the RCM matrix.

kpis.name: Strategies in Use
kpis.formula: Count of distinct values in the strategy field across RCM_MATRIX.
kpis.rules: Exclude blank and retired assignments.

kpis.name: Most-Assigned Strategy
kpis.formula: The strategy value with the highest count across RCM_MATRIX (mode of the strategy field).
kpis.rules: If tied, display the first governed ordering/tie rule.

kpis.name: Last Framework Review
kpis.formula: Maximum approved RCM review date.
kpis.rules: Use approved review records only.

rcm.visuals: RCM table links functions, failure modes, consequences and selected strategies.
rcm.limits: RCM assignment is an engineering decision, not solely a statistical result.

opportunistic.title: Opportunistic & Outage-Based Maintenance
opportunistic.purpose: Bundles compatible tasks into planned visits or outages.
opportunistic.use: Review visit windows, bundled tasks and avoided truck rolls.

kpis.name: Upcoming Bundled Visits
kpis.formula: Count of planned future visits/outages containing two or more bundled tasks.
kpis.rules: Distinct visit IDs; exclude cancelled windows.

kpis.name: Truck-Rolls Saved
kpis.formula: Σ max(0, standalone visits represented by bundled tasks − actual bundled visits).
kpis.rules: Use approved bundling plan and avoid counting tasks already co-located by default.

kpis.name: Tasks Bundled
kpis.formula: Count of distinct maintenance tasks assigned to a bundled visit/outage.
kpis.rules: Count each task once.

kpis.name: Next Planned Outage
kpis.formula: Minimum future planned-outage start date.
kpis.rules: Exclude cancelled/completed outages.

opportunistic.visuals: Bundling table shows site, outage/visit, tasks, crew and expected savings.
opportunistic.data: Work plans, outage schedule, geography, crew and material readiness.
opportunistic.limits: Bundling must not defer safety-critical or warranty-notice work.

approval.title: Approval Workflow
approval.purpose: Provides role-based governance before recommendations become executable work.
approval.use: Select a case, review evidence/checklists and advance only when approval conditions are met.

kpis.name: Active Cases
kpis.formula: WORKFLOW_CASES.length — the total count of all workflow cases in the dataset.
kpis.rules: This is every case in the dataset, not filtered to exclude Approved/Rejected/Closed cases — despite the "Active" label, closed cases are also included in this count.
kpis.meaning: Total case volume, not specifically the open/active subset.

kpis.name: Awaiting Approval
kpis.formula: Count of active cases currently at an approval step requiring a user decision.
kpis.rules: Exclude evidence-preparation and completed steps.

kpis.name: Roles in Chain
kpis.formula: A hardcoded literal value of 6, representing the fixed role chain CRO · ME · MM · AM · HSE · FT.
kpis.rules: Not derived from a configurable workflow-role list in the current build — always displays 6.
kpis.meaning: Static demo value describing the fixed approval chain used in this build.

kpis.name: Avg. Cycle Time
kpis.formula: A hardcoded literal value of 18 hours.
kpis.rules: Not computed from case creation/decision timestamps in the current build.
kpis.meaning: Static demo value, not a live calculation.

approval.visuals: Stepper, role card, checklist and audit trail explain case progression.
approval.data: Recommendation, evidence, role, SLA and audit records.
approval.limits: Approval does not itself confirm ERP posting; review transaction status afterward.

maintenancelearning.title: Maintenance Learning
maintenancelearning.purpose: Learns from completed maintenance outcomes to identify repeatable practices.
maintenancelearning.use: Compare success, MTTR, recurrence and technician outcomes, then review learned practices.

kpis.name: Repair success
kpis.formula: 100 × outcomes where Repair_Success = Successful ÷ all maintenance outcomes.
kpis.rules: Partial and failed outcomes remain in the denominator; exclude invalid duplicate outcome IDs.

kpis.name: Average MTTR
kpis.formula: Σ Actual_Duration_Hours ÷ maintenance outcomes.
kpis.rules: Use valid completed outcomes; the screen averages the available actual-duration field.

kpis.name: 90-day recurrence
kpis.formula: 100 × outcomes where Recurrence_Within_90_Days = Yes ÷ all maintenance outcomes.
kpis.rules: Only mature outcomes should be used in production; demo uses all loaded records.
kpis.meaning: Lower means repairs are more durable.

kpis.name: Technician effectiveness
kpis.formula: Σ Technician_Effectiveness_Pct ÷ maintenance outcomes.
kpis.rules: Exclude blank/invalid effectiveness values in production; demo averages available numeric values.

maintenancelearning.visuals: Charts show success and confidence by failure mode; table shows asset class, practice, evidence and outcome rates.
maintenancelearning.data: Maintenance Outcomes and Maintenance Learning worksheets.
maintenancelearning.limits: Correlation in historical outcomes does not prove causation; require engineering review.

spares.title: Spare Parts Planning
spares.purpose: Forecasts reorder need using stock, consumption, lead time and asset-risk/RUL demand.
spares.use: Review shortage signals and planned reorders before transferring procurement action.

kpis.name: Below Reorder Point
kpis.formula: Count of SPARE_PARTS records where status ≠ "OK".
kpis.rules: This includes every non-OK status (e.g. Critical, Low), not strictly items numerically below their reorder point.
kpis.meaning: Parts flagged for attention by their status field.

kpis.name: Inventory Value
kpis.formula: Σ on-hand quantity × unit cost.
kpis.rules: Use usable on-hand stock and current governed valuation basis.

kpis.name: Avg. Supplier Lead Time
kpis.formula: Σ supplier lead-time days ÷ active parts/supplier records.
kpis.rules: Exclude missing lead times; use preferred supplier when multiple sources exist.

kpis.name: RUL-Linked Reorders
kpis.formula: Count of SPARE_PARTS records where rulBoostPct > 0 — i.e. parts whose reorder recommendation has been boosted because a predictive RUL model shortened the associated asset's remaining life.
kpis.rules: Distinct part-site recommendation IDs.

spares.visuals: Planning tables connect demand, lead time, stock and RUL exposure.
spares.data: Spare master, inventory, consumption, supplier and predictive-demand records.
spares.limits: Recommended reorder quantities require procurement and obsolescence review.

inventory.title: Spares Inventory
inventory.purpose: Shows physical stock movement and days of inventory.
inventory.use: Review quantity balances, receipts/issues and parts with low or excessive cover.

kpis.name: Closing Balance (units)
kpis.formula: Σ opening balance + receipts − issues ± approved adjustments across parts/locations.
kpis.rules: Count usable stock according to location/status rules.

kpis.name: Receipts (30d)
kpis.formula: Σ received quantity posted in the trailing 30 days.
kpis.rules: Use posted receipts; exclude cancelled/reversed transactions.

kpis.name: Issues (30d)
kpis.formula: Σ issued quantity posted in the trailing 30 days.
kpis.rules: Use posted issues net of reversals.

kpis.name: Fleet Avg. Days of Inventory
kpis.formula: Average across eligible parts of On-hand Quantity ÷ Average Daily Usage.
kpis.scope: Current stock and configured usage history
kpis.rules: Exclude parts with no valid usage or show separately as no-consumption; screen uses available DOI values.

inventory.visuals: DOI chart ranks parts by cover; inventory table shows balances and usage.
inventory.limits: Average DOI can hide critical low-stock parts; review part-level distribution.

warrantyrecovery.title: Warranty Recovery Intelligence
warrantyrecovery.purpose: Identifies claim opportunities, evidence readiness, ageing and remaining OEM coverage.
warrantyrecovery.use: Review claim pipeline and OEM exposure, then prioritise evidence-complete and time-sensitive claims.

kpis.name: Recovery opportunity
kpis.formula: Σ Claimed_Amount_INR for all loaded warranty claims/opportunities.
kpis.rules: Count each claim once; production may restrict to eligible/open statuses, while the demo sums the loaded claimed amount.
kpis.meaning: Gross value being pursued or assessed.

kpis.name: Approved recovery
kpis.formula: Σ Approved_Amount_INR across claims.
kpis.rules: Include only approved amounts recorded; exclude claimed but unapproved value.

kpis.name: Expiring in 180 days
kpis.formula: Count of warranty records whose end date is on/after the demo as-of date and less than 180 days away.
kpis.scope: 180-day forward window from demo as-of date
kpis.rules: Distinct warranty IDs; expired warranties are excluded.

kpis.name: Evidence-ready claims
kpis.formula: Count of claims where Evidence_Completeness_Pct ≥ 80.
kpis.rules: Distinct claim IDs; threshold is 80% in the screen logic.
kpis.meaning: Claims sufficiently documented for next workflow step.

warrantyrecovery.visuals: Claims pipeline counts statuses; OEM exposure sums remaining coverage; table shows amount, integer days open and evidence %.
warrantyrecovery.data: Warranty Register and Warranty Claims worksheets.
warrantyrecovery.limits: Eligibility depends on contract terms, notice windows and evidence—not KPI value alone.

crewscheduling.title: Crew Planning & Scheduling
crewscheduling.purpose: Optimises assignment using work demand, availability, skills, travel and certification constraints.
crewscheduling.use: Use assignment, board, skills, exceptions, performance, capacity and ledger tabs.

kpis.name: Crew utilization
kpis.formula: 100 × (total roster − crews marked Available) ÷ total roster.
kpis.rules: The demo infers utilisation from availability status; production should use assigned productive hours ÷ available hours.
kpis.meaning: Share of roster not currently available.

kpis.name: Available now
kpis.formula: Count of roster records whose availability contains Available; displayed against total roster.
kpis.rules: Distinct crew/person IDs.

kpis.name: Open demand
kpis.formula: Count of work orders not Closed or Completed.
kpis.rules: Distinct work-order IDs.

kpis.name: Average match
kpis.formula: Configured assignment-match score: 92 after optimisation, otherwise 84 in the demo.
kpis.rules: Production score should combine skill, certification, availability, travel, cost and priority with governed weights.

kpis.name: Schedule conflicts
kpis.formula: Assigned work orders − count of distinct assigned crew names, floored at zero.
kpis.rules: This demo proxy flags potential multiple assignments; production should evaluate overlapping time windows.

kpis.name: Certifications due
kpis.formula: Count of roster records meeting the certification-risk rule.
kpis.rules: Distinct crew/person IDs; use configured expiry-warning threshold.

crewscheduling.visuals: Tabs expose assignment recommendations, schedule, skills, exceptions, performance and capacity.
crewscheduling.data: Open work orders, crew roster, skills, certifications and assignment ledger.
crewscheduling.limits: Optimisation quality depends on accurate calendars, travel times and skill records.

esgoverview.title: ESG Executive Overview
esgoverview.purpose: Portfolio view of renewable output, avoided carbon, water, waste, safety and ESG exceptions.
esgoverview.use: Use KPI exceptions and plant ranking to identify environmental, safety and supplier/compliance issues.

kpis.name: Renewable generation
kpis.formula: Σ generation MWh ÷ 1,000.
kpis.rules: Sum valid generation records once.

kpis.name: Carbon emissions avoided
kpis.formula: Σ the pre-populated avoided-emissions field across all ESG Monthly records in the loaded dataset.
kpis.rules: This screen sums an existing per-record field; it does not itself multiply generation by an emission factor.

kpis.name: Water consumption intensity
kpis.formula: 1,000 × Σ water consumption (kL) ÷ Σ generation (MWh).
kpis.rules: Generation must be positive; include governed operational/cleaning water.

kpis.name: Waste diversion
kpis.formula: 100 × Σ diverted waste ÷ Σ total waste.
kpis.rules: Exclude unclassified waste only if methodology states so.

kpis.name: Lost-time injuries
kpis.formula: Σ lost-time injury count.
kpis.rules: Count distinct incidents, not lost days.

kpis.name: ESG exceptions
kpis.formula: Count of compliance records with Action Required + count of suppliers rated High risk.
kpis.rules: The same issue must not appear in both populations unless genuinely separate.

esgoverview.visuals: Monthly charts show avoided carbon and water intensity; table ranks plant exceptions.
esgoverview.data: ESG Monthly, compliance, supplier, climate and target records.
esgoverview.limits: Demo metrics are operational indicators, not an assured disclosure report.

carbonwater.title: Clean Energy, Carbon & Water
carbonwater.purpose: Examines generation attainment, losses, avoided emissions and water circularity.
carbonwater.use: Compare expected versus actual generation and review cleaning effectiveness.

kpis.name: Generation attainment
kpis.formula: 100 × Σ actual generation ÷ Σ expected generation.
kpis.rules: Expected generation must be valid and positive.

kpis.name: Downtime loss
kpis.formula: Σ downtime-related generation loss.
kpis.rules: Use attributed loss records and prevent overlap with curtailment.

kpis.name: Curtailment
kpis.formula: Σ curtailment-related energy loss.
kpis.rules: Include only confirmed curtailment attribution.

kpis.name: Avoided emissions
kpis.formula: Σ avoided-emissions field.
kpis.rules: Use approved grid factor.

kpis.name: Carbon emissions avoided
kpis.formula: Σ avoided-emissions field; this duplicates the preceding avoided-emissions measure in the current screen.
kpis.rules: Both displayed cards use the same source calculation in this HTML.
kpis.meaning: Same avoided-carbon total shown under a second label.

kpis.name: Recycled water share
kpis.formula: 100 × Σ recycled water ÷ Σ total water consumption.
kpis.rules: Total water must be positive; recycled volume must be within total.

carbonwater.visuals: Generation chart compares expected and actual; water chart ranks plants; cleaning table links water to PR recovery.
carbonwater.limits: The two avoided-carbon cards currently calculate the same value.

circularity.title: Circularity & Asset End-of-Life
circularity.purpose: Tracks waste, recovery, e-waste, hazardous waste and certificates.
circularity.use: Review recovery rate and unresolved certificate exceptions.

kpis.name: Waste generated
kpis.formula: Σ total waste quantity.
kpis.rules: Use governed waste boundary and avoid duplicate manifests.
kpis.meaning: Total material leaving operations as waste.

kpis.name: Recovered
kpis.formula: Σ waste reused, recycled or otherwise recovered.
kpis.rules: Include only documented recovery routes.

kpis.name: Circularity rate
kpis.formula: 100 × recovered waste ÷ waste generated.
kpis.rules: Total waste must be positive.

kpis.name: E-waste
kpis.formula: Σ e-waste quantity.
kpis.rules: Use authorised category mapping.

kpis.name: Hazardous waste
kpis.formula: Σ hazardous-waste quantity.
kpis.rules: Classify per applicable regulation.

kpis.name: Certificate exceptions
kpis.formula: Count of waste movements/records missing or failing required disposal/recycling certificate validation.
kpis.rules: Distinct exception IDs.

circularity.visuals: Charts and tables show waste categories, recovery routes and certificate status.
circularity.limits: Recovery claims require valid downstream evidence.

hseclimate.title: HSE, Climate Risk & Compliance
hseclimate.purpose: Combines safety incidents, actions, physical climate exposure and compliance.

kpis.name: Lost-time incidents
kpis.formula: Count of distinct incidents classified as lost-time.
kpis.rules: Count incidents, not lost days.

kpis.name: Recordable events
kpis.formula: Count of incidents meeting recordability criteria.
kpis.rules: Apply governed regulatory/company definition.

kpis.name: Near misses
kpis.formula: Count of reported near-miss events.
kpis.rules: Deduplicate reports for one event.

kpis.name: Open HSE actions
kpis.formula: Count of HSE actions not Closed/Completed.
kpis.rules: Distinct action IDs.

kpis.name: High-Risk Plants
kpis.formula: 100 × (count of plants with Composite_Climate_Risk_Score ≥ 0.70) ÷ (total plants with a climate risk score).
kpis.rules: The card displays a percentage, not a raw count — the underlying count is shown as supporting text beneath the value (e.g. "3 of 12 plants").
kpis.meaning: Share of the portfolio currently in the high physical-climate-risk band.

kpis.name: Compliance actions
kpis.formula: Count of open compliance actions.
kpis.rules: Exclude closed/cancelled actions.

hseclimate.visuals: Incident/action tables and climate ranking connect operational safety with resilience.
hseclimate.data: HSE incidents, actions, climate risk and compliance registers.
hseclimate.limits: Climate scores are scenario-dependent, not forecasts of exact events.

executiveperformance.title: Executive Performance
executiveperformance.purpose: Connects generation, revenue, recovery potential and site status.
executiveperformance.use: Use the summary to prioritise sites with the largest recovery potential and critical status.

kpis.name: Actual generation
kpis.formula: Σ Actual_Generation_MWh across executive portfolio records.
kpis.rules: Sum each plant-period record once.

kpis.name: Generation vs budget
kpis.formula: 100 × (Σ actual generation − Σ budget generation) ÷ Σ budget generation.
kpis.rules: Budget must be positive.

kpis.name: Revenue vs budget
kpis.formula: Σ Revenue_Actual_INR − Σ Revenue_Budget_INR.
kpis.rules: Use consistent recognition/budget period.

kpis.name: Recoverable generation
kpis.formula: Σ Recoverable_Generation_MWh.
kpis.rules: Include only quantified controllable recovery.

kpis.name: Recoverable revenue
kpis.formula: Σ Recoverable_Revenue_INR.
kpis.rules: Avoid double counting recovery opportunities.

kpis.name: Critical sites
kpis.formula: Count of sites where Executive_Status = Critical.
kpis.rules: Latest status per plant.

executiveperformance.visuals: Executive site table shows generation/revenue variance, PR, availability, recovery and action.
executiveperformance.data: Executive Portfolio Summary worksheet or synthetic equivalent.
executiveperformance.limits: Recoverable values are estimates until action and verification.

rootcause.title: Event & Root Cause Intelligence
rootcause.purpose: Reconstructs event chains and ranks root causes with confidence and impact.
rootcause.use: Select incident chains, review chronology, then compare root-cause findings and recommended action.

kpis.name: Active events
kpis.formula: Count of records in the current Event Log dataset.
kpis.rules: Distinct event IDs; the current screen does not apply a closed-event filter.

kpis.name: Critical events
kpis.formula: Count of event records where Severity = Critical.
kpis.rules: Distinct event IDs.

kpis.name: Generation loss
kpis.formula: Σ Generation_Loss_MWh (or recognised alias) across events.
kpis.rules: Avoid duplicate loss when multiple alarms belong to one incident in production.

kpis.name: RCA confidence
kpis.formula: Σ RCA Confidence % ÷ RCA findings.
kpis.rules: Exclude missing confidence; current demo averages available findings.
kpis.meaning: Average confidence of ranked root-cause findings.

rootcause.visuals: Root-cause distribution counts findings; event reconstruction shows chronological chains; table aggregates cause, confidence, action and revenue impact.
rootcause.data: Event Log and Root Cause Analysis worksheets.
rootcause.limits: Confidence expresses evidence strength, not proof of causation.

assetrelationships.title: Asset Relationship Intelligence
assetrelationships.purpose: Uses a knowledge graph to connect assets, failures, work, people, spares, OEMs, weather and evidence.
assetrelationships.use: Explore the graph, inspect similar cases, simulate scenarios, propose relationships and review governance.

kpis.name: Graph entities
kpis.formula: Count of records in Graph Entities.
kpis.rules: Distinct Entity_ID records.
kpis.meaning: Number of nodes available to the graph.

kpis.name: Relationships
kpis.formula: Count of Graph Relationships plus relationships created locally in the current session.
kpis.rules: Each relationship row is counted once.

kpis.name: Average confidence
kpis.formula: Σ relationship Confidence_Pct ÷ relationships.
kpis.rules: Exclude missing confidence; current demo divides by at least one to avoid zero division.
kpis.meaning: Average evidence confidence of graph edges.

kpis.name: High-risk entities
kpis.formula: Count of entities where Risk_Score ≥ 65.
kpis.rules: Threshold is 65 in current screen logic.

assetrelationships.visuals: Five tabs cover explorer, similar cases, scenario simulation, relationship builder and evidence/governance.
assetrelationships.data: Graph Entities, Graph Relationships, Graph Evidence, Graph Similar Cases, Graph Simulations and Graph Governance.
assetrelationships.limits: Inferred edges must remain distinguishable from confirmed relationships.

lossintelligence.title: Generation & Revenue Loss Intelligence
lossintelligence.purpose: Attributes expected-to-actual generation loss by cause and plant.
lossintelligence.use: Use the bridge and ranking to separate recoverable from external loss.

kpis.name: Expected generation
kpis.formula: Σ Weather_Adjusted_Expected_MWh.
kpis.rules: Sum each plant-period record once.

kpis.name: Actual generation
kpis.formula: Σ Actual_Generation_MWh.
kpis.rules: Use same plant-period boundary as expected.

kpis.name: Total loss
kpis.formula: Σ expected generation − Σ actual generation.
kpis.rules: The displayed card uses portfolio difference; detailed cause fields should reconcile.

kpis.name: Attainment
kpis.formula: 100 × Σ actual generation ÷ Σ expected generation.
kpis.rules: Expected generation must be positive.

lossintelligence.visuals: Loss bridge ranks drivers; site table separates total, recoverable and external loss.
lossintelligence.data: Generation Loss Attribution worksheet or synthetic equivalent.
lossintelligence.limits: Attribution categories must be mutually reconciled to avoid double counting.

siteperformance.title: Site Performance Ranking
siteperformance.purpose: Ranks sites by generation variance and recovery potential.
siteperformance.use: Use the league table to identify the worst-performing and highest-recovery sites.
siteperformance.visuals: This screen has no headline KPI cards. Its table columns are Rank, Site, Capacity, Generation variance, Revenue variance, Recoverable generation, Recoverable revenue and Owner.
siteperformance.data: Executive Portfolio Summary worksheet or synthetic equivalent.
siteperformance.limits: Ranking is driven by the table sort logic; no additional KPI should be inferred.

commercialppa.title: Commercial & PPA Intelligence
commercialppa.purpose: Connects contract/ERP financial data with energy delivery.
commercialppa.use: Review plant-level shortfall, penalties, receivables and curtailment compensation.

kpis.name: Invoice value
kpis.formula: Σ Invoice_Amount_INR.
kpis.rules: Sum each invoice/PPA record once.

kpis.name: Receivables
kpis.formula: Σ Receivable_Balance_INR.
kpis.rules: Use open balance net of receipts/adjustments.

kpis.name: Penalty exposure
kpis.formula: Σ Availability_Penalty_INR.
kpis.rules: Use recorded/estimated penalty fields under contract rules.

kpis.name: Curtailment compensation
kpis.formula: Σ Curtailment_Compensation_INR.
kpis.rules: Include only contract-eligible compensation.

commercialppa.visuals: PPA table shows tariff, scheduled/delivered energy, shortfall, penalty, receivable and age.
commercialppa.data: Commercial & PPA worksheet or synthetic equivalent.
commercialppa.limits: ERP/contract system remains source of truth for settlement.

managementactions.title: Management Actions
managementactions.purpose: Consolidates decision and execution actions across modules.
managementactions.use: Use owners, due dates and value at stake to drive follow-through.

kpis.name: Open actions
kpis.formula: Count of actions whose Action_Status is not Closed.
kpis.rules: Current code treats every non-Closed status as open.

kpis.name: Value at stake
kpis.formula: Σ Financial_Impact_INR across all action records.
kpis.rules: Current screen sums all records, not only open actions.

kpis.name: Critical actions
kpis.formula: Count of actions where Risk_Level = Critical.
kpis.rules: Distinct action IDs.

kpis.name: Overdue Actions
kpis.formula: Count of non-Closed actions with Due_Date earlier than today.
kpis.rules: Use valid ISO-comparable due dates.

managementactions.visuals: Decision queue shows source issue, recommendation, energy/financial impact, decision role, owner, due date and status.
managementactions.data: Management Actions worksheet or synthetic equivalent.
managementactions.limits: The current Value at Stake card includes all action records; filter logic should be governed in production.

models.title: AI Model Registry
models.purpose: Governance inventory of load-bearing, supporting, shadow and planned models.
models.use: Filter and inspect model role, status, capability and deployment rationale.

kpis.name: Load-bearing now
kpis.formula: Count of model records where deploymentRole = Load-bearing now.
kpis.rules: Distinct model/version records.

kpis.name: Supporting production
kpis.formula: Count of models with status = Production minus load-bearing-now models.
kpis.rules: Assumes load-bearing models are included in Production.

kpis.name: Shadow / validation
kpis.formula: Count of model records where status = Shadow.
kpis.rules: Distinct model/version records.
kpis.meaning: Models under validation without load-bearing authority.

kpis.name: Roadmap
kpis.formula: Count of model records where status = Planned.
kpis.rules: Distinct planned model entries.

models.visuals: Charts group models by category and deployment status; registry rows expose model details and rationale.
models.limits: Registry count does not imply every model is simultaneously active on every asset.

integrations.title: Enterprise Integrations
integrations.purpose: Shows operational connections, payloads, data flow and live event simulation.
integrations.use: Review connector status, cadence, ownership and event stream.
integrations.visuals: This screen uses integration cards, flow diagrams and event stream rather than headline KPI cards.
integrations.data: Integration configuration and simulated connector events.
integrations.limits: Standalone demo connections are simulated; production credentials require a secure backend.

climateintelligence.title: Climate Intelligence APIs
climateintelligence.purpose: Configures external physical-climate providers and converts hazard outputs into APM actions.
climateintelligence.use: Review providers, scenario, horizon and hazards, then configure site-level assessment.

kpis.name: Configured providers
kpis.formula: Count of providers in climateApiConfig.providers.
kpis.rules: Count configured provider entries.
kpis.meaning: Number of climate data/model sources configured.

kpis.name: Assessment scenario
kpis.formula: Current climateApiConfig.scenario value.
kpis.rules: This is a selected classification, not a calculated KPI.

kpis.name: Assessment horizon
kpis.formula: Current climateApiConfig.horizon value.
kpis.rules: Displayed as configured horizon.

kpis.name: Hazards selected
kpis.formula: Count of entries in climateApiConfig.hazards.
kpis.rules: Count distinct selected hazard types.

climateintelligence.visuals: Provider panel and flow strip show how hazard APIs map to site exposure and APM actions.
climateintelligence.data: Climate API configuration and provider outputs.
climateintelligence.limits: Scenario outputs are conditional assessments, not exact forecasts.

dataexplorer.title: Asset Intelligence Studio
dataexplorer.purpose: Natural-language exploration of the currently loaded dataset.
dataexplorer.use: Use supported questions and validate answers against source tables.
dataexplorer.visuals: This screen is an assistant/query interface and has no headline KPI cards.
dataexplorer.data: Current synthetic, bundled Excel or uploaded workbook data.
dataexplorer.limits: Offline responses are limited to implemented intents and available fields.

datamanagement.title: Data Management
datamanagement.purpose: Loads, validates and switches data used by the application.
datamanagement.use: Upload a supported workbook, review sheets/errors and select the active dataset.
datamanagement.visuals: This screen uses upload, validation, sheet-list and connector controls; it has no headline KPI cards.
datamanagement.data: Synthetic dataset, bundled Excel data and validated uploaded workbook.
datamanagement.limits: Schema, units and identifiers must match supported mappings; upload does not alter source systems.

decisionintelligence.title: Decision Intelligence
decisionintelligence.purpose: Consolidates existing AI recommendations from across the platform (predictive risk, prescriptive actions, warranty, inventory, etc.) into one prioritised, filterable queue for review — without altering the source data or workflow in the module each decision came from.
decisionintelligence.use: Filter by priority or category, search, then open the source module via the Action column to actually act on a decision. This screen is read-only triage, not a place to approve or execute anything itself.

kpis.name: Prioritized Decisions
kpis.formula: rows.length — the count of rows returned by buildDecisionIntelligenceRows(), which consolidates recommendations already generated elsewhere in the app.
kpis.rules: Read-only consolidation; does not create new recommendations of its own.
kpis.meaning: Total size of the ranked decision queue below.

kpis.name: Critical Decisions
kpis.formula: Count of rows where priority === "Critical".
kpis.rules: Same three-tier priority values (Critical/High/Medium) used elsewhere in the app.
kpis.meaning: How many items need governance attention first.

kpis.name: Quantified Opportunity
kpis.formula: Σ impactValue across all rows.
kpis.rules: Sums whatever financial impact value each source module already attached to its recommendation — inherits any placeholder/illustrative values from those source screens rather than recomputing them.
kpis.meaning: Combined avoided-loss and recovery potential represented by the queue.

kpis.name: Average AI Confidence
kpis.formula: Σ confidence ÷ rows.length, rounded.
kpis.rules: Simple unweighted average across all rows regardless of category.
kpis.meaning: How strong the evidence is behind the queue on average.

decisionintelligence.visuals: Ranked Decision Queue table with priority, rationale, business impact, confidence meter, source module and a one-click Action button that navigates to the originating screen. Footer shows the Detect → Diagnose → Decide → Approve → Execute → Learn governance flow as a static reference strip.
decisionintelligence.data: Built by buildDecisionIntelligenceRows(), which reads from the predictive, prescriptive, warranty and other modules' already-generated recommendation data.
decisionintelligence.limits: This is a consolidation view only — approving, rejecting or executing a decision must happen in its own source module (Approval Workflow, Work Order Intelligence, etc.), not here.

glossary.def: A recommendation generated elsewhere in the app (predictive maintenance, prescriptive actions, warranty, etc.) and pulled into one queue here for prioritised review — the underlying data still lives in and is owned by its source screen.

financialimpact.title: Financial Impact
financialimpact.purpose: Rolls up value-opportunity estimates (revenue protection, avoided maintenance cost, warranty recovery, inventory efficiency, generation-recovery potential and risk exposure) from across the platform into one commercial view, with an indicative ROI and payback for the estimated action cost.
financialimpact.use: Start with the four headline KPIs, then use the Value Opportunity by Lever chart and Financial Impact Register table to see which lever and which source module each number comes from before taking it to a management review.

kpis.name: Gross Value Opportunity
kpis.formula: Revenue at risk + avoided maintenance + warranty recovery + annual carrying-cost opportunity + generation recovery potential (deferred-risk exposure is deliberately excluded from this total).
kpis.rules: Sums five of the six rows shown in the Financial Impact Register — the sixth, "Cost of deferred intervention", is risk exposure and is shown separately, not folded into this total.
kpis.meaning: Total quantified upside available across all levers.

kpis.name: Net Expected Benefit
kpis.formula: max(0, Gross Value Opportunity − Estimated Action Cost).
kpis.rules: Floored at zero; cannot go negative on screen even if action cost exceeds gross opportunity.
kpis.meaning: What's left after paying for the actions needed to realise the opportunity.

kpis.name: Indicative ROI
kpis.formula: If action cost > 0: (Net Expected Benefit ÷ Action Cost) × 100. If action cost = 0 and gross opportunity > 0: fixed at 100%.
kpis.rules: Action cost itself is a modelled estimate (see Estimated Action Cost below), so ROI inherits that estimate's uncertainty.
kpis.meaning: Indicative return, not an audited financial ROI.

kpis.name: Indicative Payback
kpis.formula: If net benefit and action cost are both > 0: min(36, (Action Cost ÷ Net Benefit) × 12) months. Otherwise fixed at 1 month if gross opportunity > 0, else 0.
kpis.rules: Capped at 36 months regardless of the underlying math.
kpis.meaning: Indicative time to recover the estimated action cost.

kpis.name: Estimated Action Cost
kpis.formula: Sum of each prescriptive recommendation's explicit actionCost/estimatedCost field if any are present; otherwise falls back to 28% of each recommendation's costAvoided value as a modelled proxy.
kpis.rules: The 28% figure is a fixed assumption in the code, not derived from any cost dataset.
kpis.meaning: Feeds directly into ROI and payback — if no explicit cost data exists, both of those numbers rest entirely on this one hardcoded 28% assumption.

financialimpact.visuals: Value Opportunity by Lever horizontal bar chart; Commercial Snapshot breakdown card; Financial Impact Register table with calculation basis and a direct link to each lever's source screen (Work Order Intelligence, Prescriptive Maintenance, Warranty Recovery, Spares Planning, Site Performance, Predictive Maintenance).
financialimpact.data: Derived entirely from other screens' already-computed values: open critical work orders, prescriptive recommendations' cost-avoided/action-cost fields, warranty claims, spare-parts stock/reorder levels, plant PR figures and risk-asset scores.
financialimpact.limits: Values are indicative management estimates, not accounting entries — this screen never posts to ERP, changes a work order or writes back to source data. Revenue at risk uses a fixed ₹4,500/MWh tariff assumption; generation-recovery potential uses a fixed ₹4,500/MWh and 1550 hours/MW/year assumption — neither is read from an actual tariff schedule.

glossary.def: Gross Value Opportunity is the total upside before subtracting the cost of the actions needed to capture it; Net Expected Benefit is what's left after that cost.
When a recommendation doesn't have an explicit cost figure, this screen estimates one as 28% of its avoided-cost value — a fixed assumption, not a real cost estimate.

scenariosimulator.title: Scenario Analysis
scenariosimulator.purpose: A controlled what-if sandbox for comparing management decisions (maintenance timing, cleaning schedule, repair-vs-replace) side by side, using adjustable assumption sliders, without touching any real data.
scenariosimulator.use: Pick one of the three scenario types, adjust the assumption sliders, then compare the option cards, Net Value Comparison chart, Decision Comparison Matrix and Sensitivity Analysis before opening the recommended action's source screen.
scenariosimulator.visuals: Scenario selector (Maintenance Timing / Module Cleaning Optimization / Repair vs Replace); assumption sliders; option cards with per-option metrics; Net Value Comparison bar chart; Decision Comparison Matrix table; Recommendation Confidence ring; collapsible Calculation Assumptions list; Sensitivity Analysis bars; Executive Decision Summary.
scenariosimulator.data: Uses live plant PR/availability/MW figures and risk-asset data as a starting context, then applies the slider-adjusted assumptions through scenario-specific formulas (not tied to any single external dataset).
scenariosimulator.limits: This screen has no headline KPI cards of its own — it's an interactive comparison tool. Slider inputs never alter synthetic data, uploaded Excel data, work orders, financial metrics or ERP/EAM records — every result resets when you reset or leave the screen. The AI recommendation is explicitly labelled indicative and must be validated against engineering constraints, contractual obligations, OEM guidance and approved financial assumptions before execution.

glossary.def: One of three predefined management decision types (maintenance timing, cleaning schedule, repair vs replace) that this screen can simulate; each has its own set of adjustable assumptions and comparison metrics.
Shows which input assumption has the most relative influence on the recommended outcome — a way to see which slider matters most before trusting the recommendation.

decisiontraceability.title: Decision Traceability & Explainability
decisiontraceability.purpose: Shows the complete evidence chain behind a single AI-driven decision — from the originating sensor signal through to the expected financial benefit — so each step can be traced back to its source screen.
decisiontraceability.use: Select a decision in the Decision Register, then read the Decision Evidence Chain top to bottom; each step opens the module that actually produced that evidence. Top Influencing Variables and Model & Assumptions give the reasoning behind the recommendation.

kpis.name: Traceable decisions
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of 24 in the template.
kpis.rules: Not counted from any live decision dataset in the current build.

kpis.name: Evidence completeness
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of 96.00%.
kpis.rules: Not computed from any evidence-tracking data.

kpis.name: Average confidence
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of 88.40%.
kpis.rules: Not averaged from any live confidence data — separate from the per-decision confidence values shown lower on the same screen, which do come from the RIGOUR_DECISIONS demo array.

kpis.name: Unexplained decisions
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of 0.
kpis.rules: Always displays zero regardless of any actual governance exceptions.

decisiontraceability.visuals: Decision Register table (3 demo decisions, clickable); Decision Evidence Chain (9-step trace with unit and source per step, each step clickable to its origin screen); Top Influencing Variables bar list; Model & Assumptions table.
decisiontraceability.data: The three decisions, their evidence-chain steps, influencing-variable weights and model metadata are all fixed demo content defined directly in the render function (RIGOUR_DECISIONS array and a hardcoded trace array) — none of it is read from ALL_WOS, PLANTS, RISK_ASSETS or any other live dataset.
decisiontraceability.limits: Every number on this screen — the four KPI cards, the influencing-variable percentages, the model confidence and the evidence-chain values — is static demo content, not a live calculation. Treat this screen as an illustration of what an evidence chain would look like, not as real audit data.

glossary.def: The sequence of data points and modules (SCADA signal → event correlation → AI detection → prediction → financial impact → scenario → recommendation → work order → benefit) that together justify one AI-driven decision, each traceable back to its source.

A relative percentage contribution to a specific recommendation, not a probability — the variable with the highest percentage had the largest effect on that particular decision, not on decisions generally.

closedloopexecution.title: Closed-Loop Execution
closedloopexecution.purpose: Tracks how AI recommendations flow through to completion — Detected → Recommended → Approved → Scheduled → Executed → Verified → Benefits Realized — as a funnel, plus a register of individual decisions at each stage.
closedloopexecution.use: Read the Execution Lifecycle funnel to see where decisions are piling up or dropping off, then use the Execution Register to open a specific decision, its work order, or its realised benefit.

kpis.name: Open recommendations
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of 24.
kpis.rules: Matches the "Detected" stage count in the funnel array, also hardcoded.

kpis.name: Approval rate
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of 81.82%.
kpis.rules: Not computed from the funnel counts shown on the same screen (18 Approved ÷ 22 Recommended would actually be 81.8%, so this happens to be internally consistent, but it is still a typed-in literal, not a live division).

kpis.name: Execution on time
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of 86.67%.
kpis.rules: Not computed from any schedule-vs-actual data.

kpis.name: Benefits verified
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of ₹44.30 lakh.
kpis.rules: Not summed from the Execution Register rows shown on the same screen.

closedloopexecution.visuals: Execution Lifecycle funnel (7 stages, each a fixed count, clickable to scroll to the register); Execution Register table of 5 demo decisions with status, work order and expected benefit, each field clickable to its source screen.
closedloopexecution.data: The funnel stage counts and the five register rows are fixed demo arrays defined directly in the render function — not derived from ALL_WOS or any other live dataset.
closedloopexecution.limits: Every number on this screen is static demo content. The funnel stage counts do not sum or reconcile against any live work-order population.

glossary.def: The seven governed stages a recommendation passes through from being detected to having its benefit realised; a smaller count at each successive stage is expected (some items wait, get rejected, or aren't yet verified) and is not itself a problem.

benefitsrealization.title: Benefits Realization
benefitsrealization.purpose: Compares the benefit predicted for a completed action against what was actually verified afterward, by value lever and by individual decision, with the verification controls required before a benefit can be recognised.
benefitsrealization.use: Check the Realization Rate KPI first, then Predicted vs Actual by Value Lever to see which lever under- or over-delivered, then the Benefits Realization Register to trace an individual decision back to its Decision Traceability record.

kpis.name: Predicted benefit
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of ₹54.30 lakh.
kpis.rules: Not summed from the five value-lever rows or the five register rows shown on the same screen.

kpis.name: Actual verified benefit
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of ₹42.30 lakh.
kpis.rules: Not summed from the register rows shown on the same screen.

kpis.name: Realization rate
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of 77.90%, labelled as actual ÷ predicted.
kpis.rules: 42.30 ÷ 54.30 ≈ 77.9%, so the number is internally consistent with the two KPIs above it, but all three are independently typed-in literals, not a live calculation chain.

kpis.name: Recommendation adoption
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of 81.82%.
kpis.rules: Same literal value as "Approval rate" on the Closed-Loop Execution screen.

benefitsrealization.visuals: Predicted vs Actual by Value Lever bar chart (5 levers, bar length = actual as % of predicted); Verification Controls checklist; Benefits Realization Register table (5 demo decisions) linking back to Decision Traceability.
benefitsrealization.data: The value-lever figures and register rows are fixed demo arrays defined directly in the render function.
benefitsrealization.limits: Every number on this screen is static demo content, not computed from live work-order or financial data. The methodology described (weather-normalised actuals, Finance/O&M validation before recognition, double-counting checks) describes the intended production process, not something this build actually executes.

glossary.def: Verified actual benefit divided by approved predicted benefit — the core measure of whether a decision delivered what it promised. Below 100% means the outcome underdelivered versus the prediction.

The governance step where a predicted benefit becomes an accepted actual figure, gated on baseline approval, a complete measurement window, weather normalisation (for generation-related benefits) and finance validation.

reliabilityengineering.title: Operational Reliability
reliabilityengineering.purpose: Fleet-wide reliability view by asset class — MTBF, MTTR, technical availability and failure-mode distribution — intended to support reliability-centred maintenance decisions.
reliabilityengineering.use: Check the four headline KPIs, then Failure Distribution and Reliability Growth for trend context, then the Asset-Class Reliability Register to drill into a specific asset class's predictive-maintenance evidence.

kpis.name: Fleet MTBF
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of 4,987 hours.
kpis.rules: Not computed from any failure-interval data.

kpis.name: Fleet MTTR
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of 5.42 hours.
kpis.rules: Not computed from any restoration-time data — a separate, differently-computed MTTR trend exists on the Corrective Maintenance screen.

kpis.name: Technical availability
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of 97.84%.
kpis.rules: Distinct from the live Availability KPI on Overview/Site Performance, which is computed from PLANTS[].availability.

kpis.name: Criticality coverage
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of 100.00%.
kpis.rules: Always shows full coverage regardless of actual asset criticality classification.

reliabilityengineering.visuals: Failure Distribution bar list (5 failure modes, clickable to Event & Root Cause Intelligence); Reliability Growth index trend (4 quarters); Asset-Class Reliability Register table (6 asset classes, clickable to Predictive Maintenance).
reliabilityengineering.data: All figures — the six-asset-class register, the failure-distribution percentages and the quarterly growth index — are fixed demo arrays defined directly in the render function.
reliabilityengineering.limits: Every number on this screen is static demo content, not computed from ALL_WOS, ASSET_REGISTRY or any other live dataset. The Reliability Growth index is explicitly labelled an index (not a probability or percentage) combining MTBF improvement, MTTR reduction and repeat-failure reduction, but no such combination is actually calculated in this build.

glossary.def: Mean Time Between Failures — average operating time between functional failures for an asset population; higher is more reliable.
Mean Time To Repair/Restore — average time from failure to return-to-service; lower is better, but should be read together with recurrence rate so speed isn't rewarded over quality.
Whether equipment was capable of operating, independent of how it performed — distinct from the site-level Availability KPI used elsewhere in the app.

portfoliobenchmarking.title: Portfolio Benchmarking
portfoliobenchmarking.purpose: Ranks the portfolio's sites against each other on a single composite score blending performance, cost and reliability, to surface leaders and sites needing management attention.
portfoliobenchmarking.use: Check the Composite Site Ranking and headline KPIs, use the Benchmark Interpretation thresholds to read the score bands, then the Site Benchmark Register for the underlying per-site figures.

kpis.name: Top-performing site
kpis.formula: The first site (highest composite score) from a locally-built list of up to 8 sites, each site's score computed as max(60, 94 − index×4) where index is the site's position after sorting by PLANTS[] order (i.e. score is set by array position, not by an independent calculation).
kpis.rules: The score formula is a simple descending step function tied to list order, not the composite formula described in the Composite Site Ranking chart below it (PR 25% / availability 20% / failure rate 20% / O&M cost 15% / inventory 10% / productivity 10%) — the two are inconsistent with each other in this build.
kpis.meaning: Points at the site the demo has arbitrarily ranked #1; the displayed weighting methodology is illustrative, not what actually produced this number.

kpis.name: Portfolio median PR
kpis.formula: Despite the name, this is the mean (average) of the PR values for the up-to-8 sites included, not the statistical median.
kpis.rules: Uses PLANTS[].pr where available, otherwise a synthetic fallback (78 − index×0.3).
kpis.meaning: Labelled median but actually an average — do not treat it as a true median.

kpis.name: Best availability
kpis.formula: max() of the availability values across the up-to-8 included sites.
kpis.rules: Uses PLANTS[].availability where available, otherwise a synthetic fallback (97.5 − index×0.2).
kpis.meaning: The single highest availability figure among the benchmarked sites.

kpis.name: Benchmark outliers
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of 2.
kpis.rules: Not computed from any statistical outlier detection.

portfoliobenchmarking.visuals: Composite Site Ranking bar list (clickable, currently routes to Overview regardless of which site is clicked); Benchmark Interpretation threshold table (90-100 Leading / 80-89 Competitive / 70-79 Watch / <70 Intervention); Site Benchmark Register table with cost and failure-rate columns.
portfoliobenchmarking.data: Reads live PLANTS[] data for name/PR/availability/MW where present, but the composite score, O&M cost/MW and failures/100-assets figures are synthetic formulas seeded by each site's position in the list, not independently sourced cost or failure data.
portfoliobenchmarking.limits: The composite score's stated methodology (PR 25%, availability 20%, failure rate 20%, O&M cost/MW 15%, inventory efficiency 10%, work-order productivity 10%) is not the formula actually used to produce the displayed score — the actual score is a simple rank-based step function. Cost and failure-rate figures are synthetic, not from a real O&M cost or failure dataset. All ranking bars currently link to Overview rather than to a site-specific drill-down.

glossary.def: A single 0-100 index intended to blend several performance, cost and reliability measures into one ranking number; in this build it does not actually combine those measures the way its description states.

aigovernance.title: AI Governance & Model Operations
aigovernance.purpose: Tracks model risk, drift and governance-control compliance across the platform's AI models, separate from the AI Model Registry's deployment inventory.
aigovernance.use: Check the four headline KPIs, review Governance Control Coverage for which controls are weakest, check open Governance Exceptions, then use the AI Model Operations Register to drill into a specific model on the AI Model Registry screen.

kpis.name: Production models
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of 18.
kpis.rules: Not counted from MODEL_REGISTRY or any live model-status data; a different hardcoded value (11) is shown as "Models in Production" on the Predictive Maintenance screen — the two never reconcile.

kpis.name: Healthy models
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of 16.
kpis.rules: Not computed from any drift-monitoring data.

kpis.name: Models under review
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of 2.
kpis.rules: Matches the count of "Drift"/"Review" status rows in the 6-row demo register shown on the same screen, but is itself a separate typed-in literal, not a live count.

kpis.name: Governance compliance
kpis.formula: Hardcoded literal value of 94.44%.
kpis.rules: Not computed from the Governance Control Coverage percentages shown on the same screen.

aigovernance.visuals: Governance Control Coverage bar list (6 controls: named owner, version control, approval evidence, drift monitoring, training data lineage, outcome monitoring — each a fixed percentage); Governance Exceptions table (4 fixed rows); AI Model Operations Register (6 demo models, clickable to AI Model Registry).
aigovernance.data: All figures — the 6 control-coverage percentages, the 4 exceptions and the 6-model register — are fixed demo content defined directly in the render function, not read from MODEL_REGISTRY.
aigovernance.limits: Every number on this screen is static demo content. This screen's model counts do not reconcile with the AI Model Registry screen's own counts or with Predictive Maintenance's "Models in Production" figure — treat each screen's model-count KPI as independent until the underlying data is unified.

glossary.def: When a deployed model's real-world performance degrades from what it showed during validation, typically because the data it now sees differs from its training data.

A mandatory checkpoint (named owner, version control, approval evidence, drift monitoring, training-data lineage, outcome monitoring) a production model must satisfy; coverage below 100% on any control is an open governance gap even if the model's overall status still shows Production.
